content:
alex: Heads-up — after the TF change last night, pods in telemetry namespace are failing to mount S3 creds. Can someone quick-check?

infra-bot: Deploy v2.8.1 completed to telemetry-prod at 2024-11-01T03:12:10Z :rocket:

priya: Error from the pod shows token projection failure + secret mount error. Sample from `kubectl describe pod telemetry-collector-5f6d`:
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedMount  2s (x12 over 3m)  kubelet, ip-10-0-12-34  MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "s3-creds" : secret "telemetry-s3-creds" not found
  Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox  1s (x3 over 3m)  kubelet, ip-10-0-12-34  Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to get token: TokenRequest failed: serviceaccount token projection: unauthorized
```

ben: Most likely IRSA/service-account annotation mismatch. Did the TF change rename the role or the role tag? Quick checklist: 
- check ServiceAccount annotation `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` (or `iam.amazonaws.com/role` on older charts)
- check TF-managed aws_iam_role name/arn

lisa: I noticed the TF diff replaced `role_name = "redwood-telemetry-runner"` with `role_name = "redwood-telemetry-runner-v2"` in the iam module. If the SA annotation still points to the old role ARN, pods lose permissions and the projected token request will fail.

alex: Here's what the SA looked like in the helm values (values.yaml -> telemetry.serviceAccount):
```
serviceAccount:
  create: false
  name: telemetry-runner
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-telemetry-runner
```

alex: And the TF snippet that got merged last night (in infra-iam module):
```
resource "aws_iam_role" "telemetry" {
  name = "redwood-telemetry-runner-v2"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.telemetry_assume.json
}
```

priya: So the role ARN changed. Two quick fixes: update helm/values to the new ARN or update TF to keep old role name (and reattach policies). Which do we want?

ben: Prefer to update the helm values (sa annotation) and do a rolling restart of the telemetry deployment. That avoids IAM churn. Steps I recommend:
1) patch the SA in telemetry namespace with correct annotation pointing at the new role ARN
```
kubectl -n telemetry patch sa telemetry-runner --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/metadata/annotations/eks.amazonaws.com~1role-arn","value":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-telemetry-runner-v2"}]'
```
2) restart the deployment: `kubectl -n telemetry rollout restart deploy/telemetry-collector`
3) confirm pod mounts and S3 access in logs

lisa: I'd do a canary first: patch the SA in telemetry-canary ns or patch a single replicaset if we have one. If all good, then patch prod. Also we should update the helm chart repo (values.yaml) so future deploys don't revert the annotation.

alex: I'll open a quick PR to telemetry-helm with updated values and push a separate infra PR to revert role rename if we want rollback option. Ben — can you review the Helm PR?

ben: Yup, will review. Also double-check the annotation key: some older charts use `iam.amazonaws.com/role` vs `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. Use whichever the chart expects.

priya: One more gotcha — if the cluster has projected token TTL limits, and the pods are using tokenRequest with audience, ensure the kube-apiserver feature gate isn't blocking. But in this case the secret-not-found + token failure points to annotation mismatch.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-4987 - telemetry S3 creds failure. Assigned to alex.

alex: On it. Will patch canary first and report back here with outcome. :thumbsup:
